hints.content:
We define function $f$ using a definite integral of function $h$. For every $x$-value, we calculate $f(x)$ by taking the definite integral of $h$ from $3$ to $x$.

So to calculate $f(\goldD{4})$ we need to take the definite integral of $h$ from $3$ to $\goldD{4}$:

$f(\goldD{4})=\displaystyle\int_{3}^{\goldD{4}}h(t)\,dt$

This represents the net area between the graph of $h(t)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=3$ to $x=4$.

We can find $\displaystyle\int_{3}^{\goldD{4}}h(t)\,dt$ using geometric area formulas.

![The graph of function h has the region between the segments and the x-axis, between x = 3 and x = 4, shaded. The segment at the top of the shaded region moves downward from (3, 7) to (4, 4).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/24fa0950c8188cf41e49c3e1bf40c9aff985e67c)

We have a $1$ by $4$ rectangle and a $1$ by $3$ right triangle, so in total the area is $5.5$.
